input: Pitch a feature article to a travel magazine

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific article topic, angle, or destination shapes the entire pitch — a niche adventure piece needs a very different pitch than a luxury travel or cultural immersion story.
Whether this is for a specific named magazine or a list of targets determines how to tailor the pitch to a particular editor, readership, and editorial style.
Knowing the user's prior publishing credits affects how they should frame their bio and credentials — a first-time pitcher needs different guidance than an experienced freelancer.
A hard submission deadline changes how much time can be spent researching the outlet, drafting, and revising before sending.
Whether the user needs help writing the full pitch email, just the article synopsis, or a query letter template determines what output to produce.
Knowing whether success means getting a response, a commission, or simply sending a polished pitch changes what 'done well' looks like and how much follow-up planning is needed.
The tone of travel writing varies enormously — lyrical and literary vs. practical and service-driven — and the pitch should mirror the style the user intends for the article.

gold.taskTitle: Pitch a feature article to a travel magazine
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to write and submit a pitch for a feature article to a travel magazine, with the goal of getting it accepted for publication.

questions.title: What specific destination or travel topic will the article cover?
questions.description: Identify the core subject of the article — a place, theme, experience, or angle — so the pitch can be built around a concrete, compelling idea.

questions.title: Which travel magazine are you targeting with this pitch?
questions.description: Pinpoint the specific publication (e.g., Condé Nast Traveler, Lonely Planet Magazine, Outside) to tailor the pitch to that outlet's tone, section, and editor.

questions.title: Have you been published before, in travel writing or elsewhere?
questions.description: Understand the user's publishing history so the credentials section of the pitch is framed appropriately for their experience level.

questions.title: Is there a submission deadline you are working toward?
questions.description: Establish whether there is a time constraint driving urgency, which shapes how much research and revision time is realistic.

questions.title: What do you need help producing — a full pitch email or just the synopsis?
questions.description: Clarify the exact deliverable: a complete query letter, a one-paragraph synopsis, a subject-line strategy, or a step-by-step plan for the whole submission process.

questions.title: What does a successful outcome look like to you here?
questions.description: Determine whether the user's goal is to send a polished pitch, receive an editor's response, secure a commission, or something else — so the plan is scoped correctly.

questions.title: What tone or style are you aiming for in the article itself?
questions.description: Identify whether the piece leans literary and personal, practical and service-driven, investigative, or humorous — the pitch should reflect and preview the article's voice.
